messages.content: What is the freezing point point of water at a pressure of 10 kPa?

function.name: thermodynamics_calculate_boiling_point

message.content:
At a pressure of about 10 kPa (≈ 0.1 atm) the freezing point of pure water drops below 0 °C.  
Using the phase‑diagram of water, the solid–liquid equilibrium line at that pressure corresponds to a temperature of roughly **–2 °C** (more precisely –2.2 °C).  

So, under a pressure of 10 kPa, water freezes at about **–2 °C**.
